title: External processors: establish provenance before execution
goal: Make a justified admission decision without executing unknown code.

prerequisites.text: 1c-enterprise.a 6; A1–A2: separate infobase, catalogs, references and documents; synthetic data only.

sections.title: A processor is executable code
paragraphs: An external processor can read/change data, access files and use available platform actions. Its extension does not make it safe; nor does a familiar sender prove unchanged content. Establish author, purpose, official source and required rights before opening anything. Never execute an unknown file out of curiosity.

EPF denotes an external data processor and ERF an external report. They can contain executable BSL; an extension is not a trust mark. This beginner course requires no “repair everything” processor: use standard cards/reports. Do not open unknown code merely to observe its behavior.

sections.title: Use existing functionality
paragraphs: Follow the scoped native application route; diagrams are not executable browser code.

code.source: Need customer minutes → standard filtered report.
code.output: The result needs no unknown processor.

sections.title: A hash binds review to a file
paragraphs: SHA256 binds a reviewed copy to later bytes; it does not itself prove harmlessness. A malicious file also has a hash. Compare against a trusted channel and attach review to that exact copy. Any modification creates new bytes requiring a new review.

An admission record identifies author/source, purpose, exact version, SHA256, expected reads/writes and reviewed environment. A hash binds review to bytes but does not establish safety. A changed file needs renewed review. An infobase copy protects source records, not arbitrary computer files or network access.

sections.title: An infobase copy does not isolate the computer
paragraphs: A copy protects source records from ordinary mistakes but does not confine code to that directory. A test infobase is not permission to run unknown BSL on the main computer. Safe mode and rights have specific contexts; full execution isolation requires an agreed boundary and evidence, not a checkbox.

Compare “show my request total” with “repair everything by disabling checks.” The first uses the existing report. The second needs a defined algorithm, scope and admission. Do not change security settings to make a file run. Sandbox is an optional engineering tool, not a required step in learning installed 1C.

sections.title: Insufficient trust evidence
paragraphs: Compare a distinct negative case while preserving accepted work.

code.output: NOT RUN: a hash proves neither content safety nor permission.

sections.title: A consultant may decline execution
paragraphs: Without a trusted source and approved environment, the outcome isNOTRUN with a reason and specialist request. That is a correct decision, not a learning failure. Practice with original teaching source and predicted actions. Execute only after admission, on synthetic data, with before/after state checks and bounded output.

This lab produces a review record and NOT RUN for an unknown file. That is a valid negative outcome, not simulated execution. A known own processor needs separate source, reproducible build and an authorized synthetic-data test, developed in the programming course. Do not publish third-party configurations or real records.

sections.title: Check your explanation
paragraphs: A known hash is treated as a safety guarantee. Bind bytes to review and separately assess author/code/permissions/environment.
An infobase copy is treated as whole-computer isolation. Separate database preservation from executable system access.
Unknown code is run to prove that it should be refused. Decide NOT RUN before execution and use the standard route.
